subject: DeltaHealth — model fit follow-up, eval artifacts, and safety Q&A
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@deltahealth.com>
Cc: Dr. Martin Shaw <martin.shaw@deltahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: DeltaHealth — model fit follow-up, eval artifacts, and safety Q&A

Thanks again for the call today, Elaine + Martin — really helpful to hear about the triage workflow and the kinds of sensitive content your clinicians want the assistant to refuse or escalate. Quick recap and proposed next steps from my side:

- Business need: near-real-time triage routing + clinician-facing summaries; strict refusal on treatment instructions and PHI exfiltration prevention.
- Immediate recommendation (tactical): run a short eval against two model classes — a compact safety-tuned 13B and a higher-capacity 70B chat model for complex summarization quality comparisons.
- Proposed models to benchmark: "Redwood-13B-safety-v2" (quantized 4-bit), and "Llama-70B-chat-q8f" (higher-capacity variant). We can also try "OpenChat-30B-instruct" if you prefer a middle ground.

What I attached/linked: a starter prompt-set (deltahealth_med_safety_prompts_v1.jsonl) with refusal scenarios and escalation triggers, plus a CSV of the eval prompt matrix (eval_prompt_set_20260320.csv). I also uploaded a short internal benchmark we ran on similar triage tasks: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/deltahealth-20260321.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Your team sends a small canonical set of 50 representative prompts (sanitized) — we can use these as the first holdout.
2) I'll loop in Rishi (infrastructure/benchmarks) and Grace (safety/controls) to scope the run and baseline the refusal/regression checks.
3) We'll deliver a short report with token-latency tradeoffs, top-line quality delta (ROUGE/clinician-blind eval), and safety false-positive/false-negative counts within 5 business days of getting the prompt set.

Open question for you: is there a preferred hosting mode for evaluation? Hosted API is fastest for an initial sweep; Dedicated pools are available if you want isolation.

Thanks — will wait for the 50 prompts and any procurement steps (procurement@deltahealth.com) if needed.

Best,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: deltahealth_med_safety_prompts_v1.jsonl (jsonl, 50 prompts) ; eval_prompt_set_20260320.csv (csv)

From: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@deltahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dr. Martin Shaw <martin.shaw@deltahealth.com>, procurement@deltahealth.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DeltaHealth — model fit follow-up, eval artifacts, and safety Q&A

Thanks Neha — that plan sounds good. A couple clarifications from our side before we send sanitized prompts:

- We can provide 50 example prompts by EOD Tuesday (mar 24). They will be de-identified but will retain domain context (symptom descriptions, triage severity).
- Our primary objective is 1) safe refusals on treatment/diagnosis prompts, 2) high-quality summarization of multi-turn clinician notes. Latency target is ~300ms p50 for short prompts; summaries can be slower if needed.
- Compliance ask: can you confirm that benchmark logs for this eval will not contain any PHI and will be stored in our tenant for audit? We prefer the Dedicated evaluation if that simplifies auditability.

One more item: procurement asked if you can share a short SDL (scope, duration, deliverables) and a draft MSA addendum for data handling during the eval.

–Elaine
Elaine Kim
Head of Clinical AI, DeltaHealth Labs
elaine.kim@deltahealth.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@deltahealth.com>, Dr. Martin Shaw <martin.shaw@deltahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DeltaHealth — model fit follow-up, eval artifacts, and safety Q&A

Looping you both in to scope the technical run — Elaine will send 50 de-identified prompts. Key asks:

- Please run parallel evals on the two model candidates listed (Redwood-13B-safety-v2 q4 + Llama-70B-chat-q8f) and include OpenChat-30B if capacity allows.
- Benchmark outputs we care about: refusal correctness (binary), hallucination incidents (annotated), summary ROUGE-L and a small clinician preference A/B (blind).
- Safety gating: implement the guarded prompt wrapper used in our safety pipeline (see docs link in related_links) and log refusal rationale.
- Regression concern: Elaine called out that prior vendors had silent quality regressions after quantization — make sure to capture model-version tags and tokenization differences so we can audit regressions across runs.

Attachments I included: deltahealth_med_safety_prompts_v1.jsonl and eval_prompt_set_20260320.csv. I also linked a short internal baseline PDF (deltahealth-benchmark-report-20260321.pdf). Please confirm estimated run time and whether Dedicated eval is required for auditable logs.

Thanks — Neha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@deltahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DeltaHealth — model fit follow-up, eval artifacts, and safety Q&A

Quick update from infra side after a 10-min look:

- We can run the three-model sweep on Hosted safely (no PHI captured) if DeltaHealth keeps data de-identified. Hosted run will be fastest — estimate ~2 hours for 50 prompts across models at a 1-token sampling config.
- For auditability/Dedicated: Dedicated gives tenant-controlled logs and KMS isolation; estimate additional setup time ~1 business day. Given procurement asks, Recommend Dedicated so DeltaHealth has full ownership of logs.
- On regression tracking: we'll tag each artifact with model git sha, tokenizer-version, quantization params (q4/q8f), and the exact kernel build. We'll produce a small regression report that highlights any quality delta vs our internal baseline (see deltahealth-benchmark-report-20260321.pdf).
- Safety guardrails: Grace, can you run the refusal rubric against the prompt set and add a short set of counterfactuals to the prompt file (I can merge) so we stress false-negative cases?

Action items:
- Neha: confirm Dedicated eval or Hosted.
- Elaine: drop the 50 de-identified prompts in the shared drive link.
- Grace: will add counterfactuals and sanity-check refusal thresholds by tomorrow morning.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
